lockFileMaintenance.description: config:recommended leaves this off, which would freeze every transitive dependency forever: caret requirements in Cargo.toml are already satisfied by the committed Cargo.lock, so nothing else ever refreshes it. CI runs --locked, so the lockfile is what actually ships.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The 7-day cooldown exists to dodge yanked releases; applying it to a published advisory would delay the fix for exactly as long as the exposure lasts.

packageRules.description: 0.x crates: under Cargo's semver rules 0.6 -> 0.7 is a breaking change, but renovate still classifies it as `minor`, so without this rule it would ride in the grouped batch above. Most of this crate's direct dependencies are 0.x. Un-grouped for the same reason as majors: isolate the break. Must stay after the grouping rule to win.
Major updates: one PR per package. A major usually breaks the API surface, so isolating each keeps the break cheap to diagnose. Automerge stays on — CI is the gate.

Rust compiler: its own PR. A bump lands new default-on clippy lints across the whole crate at once (see rust-toolchain.toml), which under -D warnings breaks CI on code that never changed. No matchDepNames filter: this manager only reads rust-toolchain.toml, so every dep it produces is the compiler, and a filter that stopped matching would silently demote the bump into another rule. Last rule wins — keep this LAST.
